doc.title: Benny Golson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Return to New York and Europe
title: German food, cars and why he chose Germany
summary: Golson loves German cooking, which he compares to Southern soul food, and says he chose Friedrichshafen because he loves it.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I love the German people, and I love the food. Those Germans cook like black people from the South. When I tell them that, they just smile. But it’s true. They cook like black people from Mississippi and North Carolina, South Carolina.

Yeah. When they bring the schwein out and the schweinebraten, oh man, I’m home. They’re so proud of it. Say, “Wirtlich?{Truly]” “Yeah.” It’s fantastic. I love that German food. Those sausages lay me out, and their bread, and their milk, and their cars. We bought an Audi there, which my wife totaled a week before we came back. I got to get another one.
I see you got a Benz out there in the drive – in the garage out here. I see you got your Benz out here in the garage.

There’s another one, the ’72. I was going to have it restored, but it’s so old. I think I’ll just sell it – somebody might want to restore it – and get a new one. But later. I’m not worried about it. We’ve got to fix this house first. Yeah, the Audi’s gone, gone. I took a picture of it. It’s all . . . People say to me, why did you move to Germany? I said, because I love it. They expect me to move to Paris or Rome. No, I’m in Friedrichshafen. We love it there.
